finding: The named consumers on feat/afkv2-s3 lose the new bad-value refusal for forge: a bad forge routes by origin, and it also removes the tracker from the tracker port.
why: The reader refuses the whole config, but `settings.read_config` on S3 turns every refusal into `{}`, so the forge port falls through to the origin remote and the tracker port reports that no tracker is configured.
fix: When S3 merges, make `ports/tracker/settings.py` pass on a reader refusal (`ok: false`, not `no-config`) as a refusal, and add a test with a bad forge through the real reader; the S3 tests stub `settings.read_config`, so they cannot catch this.
evidence: Probe: S3 `afkv2/ports` plus this head's reader in Temp, cwd is a repo with `.afkv2/config.json`. `{"spec_folder":"docs","forge":"bitbucket"}` with origin https://github.com/o/r.git gives forge kind `github`, no refusal. The same config with no origin gives `no-forge` and the reason does not name the bad key. `{"spec_folder":"docs","forge":"bitbucket","tracker":{"kind":"jira","project":"ABC"}}` gives tracker `no-tracker`: 'the repository config names no jira or github-issues tracker'; with forge `gitlab` the same config gives kind `jira`. Source: `settings.py` `return answer if isinstance(answer, dict) and answer.get("ok") else {}`; `forge_cli.py:39`. Limit: only a hand-edited config reaches this, because S3 setup writes forge only for github or gitlab (`repo_config.py:112`). The reader itself meets the contract bullet.

finding: No negative case pins the `.py` end of the `test_*v1_facts*.py` exemption, so the word 'only' in the acceptance bullet is not proved for the test-file pattern.
why: A mutant that widens the pattern to exempt any suffix passes every test, so a later edit can exempt a non-Python file such as a Markdown file without a failure.
fix: Add `tests/test_v1_facts.md` and `tests/test_v1_facts.pyi` to the parameter list of test_same_v1_name_in_any_other_file_fails; the current code already fails both names.
evidence: Probe: on a temp copy, mutant V1_FACTS_FILES = ("*v1_facts.py", "test_*v1_facts*") gave only 2 failures in the complete test_plugin_check.py: test_marketplace_lists_afkv2_beside_the_v1_plugin and test_codex_marketplace_lists_afkv2_beside_the_v1_plugin. An unmutated temp copy fails the same 2, because the copy has no repository root, so the mutant survived. The same mutation on the first pattern ("*v1_facts.*") is killed by the scripts/v1_facts.py.txt parameter. Direct probe on the current code: tests/test_v1_facts.md, .txt and .pyi each give a 'v1 name' problem. Bullet: 'exempts only files named *v1_facts.py and their test files named test_*v1_facts*.py'.

criterion: Acceptance bullet: no-v1-name exemption for v1_facts files
finding: Possible over-wide exemption: a v1 name in the file name of a v1_facts file also passes.
why: The bullet and D-46 give a reason for v1 names inside these files only, and no such file name exists on the S1, S2 or S3 branches, so AC-019 ('No afkv2 file ... uses a v1 name') loses a guard that nothing needs.
fix: Keep the file-name rule for the whole relative path of a v1_facts file, and change the test parameters that use a v1-named file to expect a file-name problem; if the owner wants the wider reading, record it in D-46.
evidence: Bullet: 'a v1 name in such a file passes'. Code: 'named_parts = relative.parent.parts if is_v1_facts else relative.parts'. Test parameters in test_v1_name_in_a_v1_facts_file_passes_both_rules_of_the_name_check: f"scripts/{V1}_v1_facts.py", f"tests/test_{V1}_v1_facts.py". git ls-tree on origin/feat/afkv2-s2 and -s3, filter v1_facts: v1_facts.py, autopilot_v1_facts.py, setup_v1_facts.py, test_tracker_v1_facts.py; none on s1. The bullet can also be read as exempting the whole file from the check, so this is a judgment call.

criterion: Acceptance bullet: config reader answers forge
finding: The reader now answers forge, but the SDD rows that describe the reader and the config file do not name that key.
why: The bullet cites SDD §8 row 'config file' for forge, and that row and the 'config reader' row do not hold it, so only D-47 records the key, while the sibling ruling D-45 did get an SDD row (line 346).
fix: Add forge (optional: github, gitlab or null) to SDD.md line 391 and line 415, in a plan or spec commit.
evidence: SDD.md:391 '| config reader | resolves `.afkv2` values (spec folder, tracker kind, ownership) |'. SDD.md:415 '| config file | `.afkv2/config.json` with a required `spec_folder`; ...'. A search of SDD.md for forge with config, key or read finds no row that names the key. Code behaviour itself meets the bullet: bad-value exit 1 and null are proved by test_config.py (529 passed, 2 xfailed with test_plugin_check.py; neither xfail is on these bullets).

finding: The `.pyi` parameter cannot fail: the check groups by the whole file name, so `sample_mod.py` and `sample_mod.pyi` never share a key, with or without the suffix filter.
why: The parameter appears to prove that `.pyi` files do not count, but that behaviour stays unproved.
evidence: Probe: on a temp copy, mutant path.suffix.lower() in (".py", ".pyi") gave only the 2 marketplace failures that an unmutated temp copy also gives, so test_init_files_tests_and_other_suffixes_do_not_count_as_a_clash passed with this parameter. Code: by_name.setdefault(name, []) with name = path.name.lower(). Direct probe on the current code: the proposed .pyi pair answers [], so the replacement parameter passes today. Not run: the replacement parameter against the mutant; by reading, the mutant gives one key with 2 paths, so it fails.

finding: The clash tests pin case folding of the file stem only, not of the suffix or of the `__init__.py` exclusion.
why: Two lowercase conversions in check_unique_module_names can be removed and no test fails.
fix: Add ("scripts/SAMPLE_MOD.PY", "engine/sample_mod.py") to the clash parameters and ["scripts/__INIT__.py", "engine/__init__.py"] to the no-clash parameters, or remove the conversions if that behaviour is not wanted.
evidence: Probe: on temp copies, mutants path.suffix == ".py" and path.name != "__init__.py" each gave only the 2 marketplace failures that an unmutated temp copy also gives, so both survived. Direct probe on the current code: the SAMPLE_MOD.PY pair reports one clash and the __INIT__.py pair answers [], so both proposed parameters pass today. Not verified: whether an uppercase suffix or __INIT__.py can occur in the plugin tree.

finding: Possible eager test: one test verifies 2 independent command behaviours, the good answer and the refusal of a bad forge.
why: A failure in the first half hides the result of the second half, and the file already keeps the good and refused read-command cases in separate tests.
fix: Split it into one test for the answered forge and one test for exit 1 on a bad forge.
